domain_label: LLM Evaluation, Benchmarking and Scoring — Benchmarks, Harnesses and Contamination
assumptions: no observed dataset or benchmark evidence supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
subdomain scope is benchmark selection, harness execution, contamination detection, metric@k selection, and leaderboard interpretation for LLM evaluation
evaluation targets instruction-tuned and base LLMs; specialized domains addressed via custom held-out benchmarks
compute budget is constrained; benchmark prioritization by signal-to-cost ratio is assumed
exclusions: data collection and annotation tooling beyond benchmark-specific IAA

competency_questions.question: Which benchmark suite should be selected to evaluate a model targeting clinical QA deployment?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BENCH_SELECTION and HELDOUT_BENCHMARK_DESIGN define capability mapping and custom benchmark need

competency_questions.question: What is the standard MMLU evaluation protocol and what does a macro-average score mean?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MMLU_PROTOCOL defines 5-shot protocol and macro-average computation

competency_questions.question: How should few-shot examples be selected and standardized for cross-model comparison?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FEWSHOT_ZEROSHOT defines shot count, example selection, and template standardization

competency_questions.question: How is GSM8K pass rate estimated with chain-of-thought and what does majority voting contribute?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: GSM8K_PROTOCOL defines CoT prompting, maj@k voting, and answer extraction

competency_questions.question: How is pass@k computed in an unbiased way and what k is appropriate for deployment?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: METRIC_AT_K defines unbiased estimator and k selection criteria

competency_questions.question: How is lm-evaluation-harness configured for reproducible benchmark execution?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LM_EVAL_HARNESS and EVAL_REPRODUCIBILITY define version pinning and config management

competency_questions.question: How does HELM differ from lm-eval-harness and when should each be used?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HELM_FRAMEWORK and LM_EVAL_HARNESS define scope differences; HELM adds calibration/fairness/toxicity

competency_questions.question: How is training data contamination of MMLU test set detected and what action follows?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CONTAMINATION_DETECTION defines n-gram method; CONTAMINATION_MITIGATION defines remediation

competency_questions.question: What statistical test should compare two models on a 164-problem benchmark like HumanEval?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: STATISTICAL_SIGNIFICANCE recommends McNemar test for paired binary outcomes with small n

competency_questions.question: How should a held-out test set be designed to have 80% power to detect a 2% accuracy difference?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HELD_OUT_TESTSET defines statistical power analysis and sample size requirements

competency_questions.question: How is LLM-as-judge evaluation validated against human raters and what biases must be mitigated?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: JUDGE_MODEL_EVAL defines position/length bias and human agreement requirement

competency_questions.question: How should an aggregate benchmark score be computed to avoid masking per-task regressions?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MULTITASK_AGGREGATE defines chance normalization and regression alerting

competency_questions.question: How should evaluation be integrated into CI/CD to prevent regressive model releases?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: EVAL_PIPELINE_CI defines regression gates and automated triggers

competency_questions.question: What should an evaluation card contain to ensure result reproducibility across labs?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: EVAL_REPRODUCIBILITY defines model SHA, harness version, dataset version, seeds, hardware spec

glossary.definition: standardized dataset and evaluation protocol measuring specific model capabilities
presence of benchmark test examples in model training data, inflating evaluation scores
probability that at least one of k generated solutions passes unit tests; estimated via unbiased Chen 2021 estimator
providing k labeled examples in the prompt before the test query to elicit in-context learning
prompting technique eliciting step-by-step reasoning traces before final answer
when a measure becomes a target it ceases to be a good measure; benchmark optimization causes benchmark to lose validity as capability proxy
average gap between model confidence and empirical accuracy across confidence bins
multi-dimensional evaluation measuring accuracy, calibration, robustness, fairness, toxicity, and efficiency simultaneously
benchmark split never used for model training, selection, or hyperparameter tuning; reserved for final evaluation only
statistical measure of label consistency across annotators; Cohen kappa is standard for categorical labels

source_registry.description: heuristic prior estimates for LLM evaluation, benchmarking, and scoring work units in absence of supplied datasets; informed by Hendrycks et al. 2020 (MMLU), Liang et al. 2022 (HELM), Chen et al. 2021 (HumanEval), Cobbe et al. 2021 (GSM8K), EleutherAI lm-eval-harness documentation, Jurafsky and Martin SLP Ch. 11
source_registry.citation_or_locator: Hendrycks 2020 arXiv:2009.03300; Liang 2022 arXiv:2211.09110; Chen 2021 arXiv:2107.03374; Cobbe 2021 arXiv:2110.14168

nodes.definition: Select task benchmarks (MMLU, GSM8K, BBH, HumanEval, ARC, HellaSwag) appropriate to model capabilities being evaluated; map benchmark coverage to capability axes; avoid benchmark-as-objective Goodhart traps.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new capability axis or benchmark released

pros.claim: Diverse benchmark suite catches capability gaps invisible to single-task eval
pros.example: MMLU alone misses code; adding HumanEval exposes coding weakness

cons.claim: Large benchmark suites incur compute cost and may reward surface-level generalism
cons.example: MMLU+BBH+HumanEval+GSM8K set may cost 100 GPU-hours per eval run

failure_modes: overfitting model development to benchmark set
ignoring out-of-scope capability gaps
selecting benchmarks misaligned to deployment task
acceptance_tests: capability axes fully covered by at least one benchmark
benchmark selection rationale documented
no benchmark used for both dev and final eval without contamination check

nodes.definition: Execute MMLU (Massive Multitask Language Understanding) evaluation: 57-subject multiple-choice QA, 5-shot standard protocol; score per-subject accuracy and macro-average; interpret domain-specific vs aggregate scores.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new MMLU version or protocol standardization changes

pros.claim: Broad 57-subject coverage of world knowledge enables cross-model comparability
pros.example: GPT-4 vs LLaMA-3 on MMLU subject breakdown reveals domain gaps

cons.claim: Multiple-choice format overestimates knowledge; models can guess without true understanding
cons.example: high MMLU score for instruction-tuned model may inflate perceived capability

failure_modes: wrong number of shots (!=5)
averaging over subjects unequally sized
prompt template mismatch across models
acceptance_tests: 5-shot prompt format verified against Hendrycks 2020 spec
all 57 subjects evaluated
macro-average computed correctly as mean of per-subject accuracies
revisit_triggers: evidence of systematic prompt sensitivity found

nodes.definition: Evaluate grade-school math reasoning with GSM8K: chain-of-thought prompting, maj@k voting, exact-match on numeric answer; assess multi-step arithmetic reasoning quality.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new math reasoning benchmark supersedes GSM8K or CoT protocol evolves

pros.claim: Tests multi-step reasoning quality; chain-of-thought traces reveal failure patterns
pros.example: wrong intermediate step in GSM8K trace pinpoints arithmetic failure type

cons.claim: GSM8K saturation at frontier models reduces discriminative power
cons.example: top models score >90% making GSM8K a near-ceiling benchmark for large models

failure_modes: majority voting instability with k<10
answer extraction regex failing on non-standard formats
prompt format causing format following rather than reasoning
acceptance_tests: answer extraction verified on 10 held-out examples
maj@k k specified and consistent across compared models
chain-of-thought enabled consistently
revisit_triggers: MATH or AIME added as harder alternative

nodes.definition: Evaluate BIG-Bench Hard (BBH): 23 hard tasks requiring multi-step reasoning beyond GPT-3 zero-shot; use 3-shot chain-of-thought; assess logical reasoning, causal inference, and compositional tasks.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: BIG-Bench benchmark updated or new hard reasoning suite released

pros.claim: BBH isolates tasks where chain-of-thought reasoning provides measurable lift
pros.example: BBH word sorting and causal judgment tasks expose reasoning chain quality

cons.claim: BBH 3-shot format may not reflect deployment zero-shot or instruction-tuned context
cons.example: 3-shot BBH scores for chat-tuned models may underestimate capability

failure_modes: using zero-shot on BBH (benchmark requires CoT)
mixing tasks with different output formats in single aggregate
acceptance_tests: 3-shot CoT prompts match Suzgun 2022 specification
all 23 tasks included in macro-average
output format parser verified per task
revisit_triggers: new hard reasoning tasks released that BBH does not cover

nodes.definition: Evaluate code generation with HumanEval: 164 Python programming problems, pass@k metric, unit test execution; assess functional correctness of generated code.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: HumanEval+ or MBPP replaces as standard; sandbox security policy changes

pros.claim: Functional correctness via unit tests is more rigorous than surface-level code similarity
pros.example: pass@1 directly measures deployment-relevant code quality

cons.claim: 164 problems insufficient for statistical stability; test cases sometimes leaked
cons.example: HumanEval contamination widespread in large-scale pretraining corpora

failure_modes: unsafe code execution without sandbox
using greedy decoding for pass@k>1
contamination from training set inflating scores
acceptance_tests: sandbox execution environment verified before any model code runs
pass@k estimator uses unbiased formula from Chen 2021
all 164 problems run without execution timeout
revisit_triggers: HumanEval contamination confirmed in model training data
MBPP or HumanEval+ adopted as standard

nodes.definition: Select and standardize few-shot vs zero-shot evaluation protocol: define k-shot count, example selection strategy (random/fixed/retrieval-based), prompt template, and instruction-tuned model adaptation; ensure protocol consistency across compared models.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: evaluation community consensus shifts on shot protocol or new benchmark standard published

pros.claim: Standardized protocol enables apples-to-apples comparison across model families
pros.example: lm-eval-harness default configs ensure reproducible few-shot setups

cons.claim: Different models favor different shot counts; fixed protocol may disadvantage certain architectures
cons.example: base models prefer few-shot; instruction-tuned prefer zero-shot with system prompt

failure_modes: mixing zero-shot and few-shot results in leaderboard
prompt template variation causing phantom performance differences
not specifying example ordering or selection randomness
acceptance_tests: shot count and template documented per benchmark
example selection strategy reproducible with fixed seed
instruction-tuned model adaptation rule specified
revisit_triggers: new instruction-tuning paradigm changes optimal shot count

nodes.definition: Deploy EleutherAI lm-evaluation-harness as standardized benchmark execution framework: task configuration, model integration (HuggingFace, API, vLLM), batch inference, results aggregation, and reproducibility via version pinning.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: lm-eval-harness major version change or task config schema update

pros.claim: Single framework for 60+ benchmarks ensures protocol consistency and community comparability
pros.example: Open LLM Leaderboard uses lm-eval-harness as canonical eval backend

cons.claim: Version pinning essential; minor version changes can shift scores by 1-3 points
cons.example: lm-eval-harness v0.3 vs v0.4 BM25 tokenization change shifted HellaSwag 1.2%

failure_modes: unpinned harness version causing irreproducibility
model tokenizer mismatch
batch size affecting generation stochasticity
acceptance_tests: harness version pinned in requirements.txt
reference model score reproduced within 0.1%
eval config YAML committed to version control
revisit_triggers: task implementation bug discovered in harness
new benchmark added requiring harness extension

nodes.definition: Apply HELM (Holistic Evaluation of Language Models): multi-metric evaluation across accuracy, calibration, robustness, fairness, bias, toxicity, and efficiency; scenario-metric matrix; trade-off visualization.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: HELM scenario set expanded or new metric dimension added

pros.claim: HELM trade-off view reveals accuracy-safety-efficiency tensions invisible to single-metric eval
pros.example: HELM shows model A is more accurate but less calibrated than model B

cons.claim: HELM compute cost is high; full evaluation suite can exceed 1000 GPU-hours per model
cons.example: HELM full suite impractical for rapid iteration cycles in development

failure_modes: cherry-picking favorable HELM metrics for reporting
ignoring calibration and fairness metrics in final model selection
acceptance_tests: all scenario categories included in HELM run
trade-off report shows accuracy vs safety dimensions
efficiency metrics recorded alongside accuracy
revisit_triggers: fairness requirements added to deployment policy

nodes.definition: Detect training data contamination of benchmark test sets: n-gram overlap analysis (8-gram), embedding similarity search, membership inference attacks, score-distribution anomaly detection; flag contaminated benchmarks for exclusion or correction.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new contamination detection method published or training data provenance changes

pros.claim: N-gram contamination detection catches verbatim benchmark leakage before scores are reported
pros.example: 8-gram overlap check on The Pile against MMLU found 5-10% test set contamination

cons.claim: Paraphrastic contamination not caught by n-gram overlap; embedding similarity computationally expensive on trillion-token corpora
cons.example: semantic contamination via paraphrase invisible to surface-level n-gram methods

failure_modes: checking only test set not train set side
not running contamination before publishing benchmark results
ignoring partial contamination that still inflates scores
acceptance_tests: 8-gram overlap check run on full training data against all benchmark test splits
contamination fraction reported per benchmark
contaminated benchmarks excluded from primary evaluation or flagged
revisit_triggers: benchmark scores suspiciously above SOTA trajectory

nodes.definition: Apply contamination mitigation: decontaminated training (exclude benchmark test n-grams), held-out variant benchmarks, dynamic evaluation generation, canary injection, and report clean vs dirty model scores separately.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new decontamination methodology published or benchmark variant becomes standard

pros.claim: Decontaminated training data enables honest benchmark comparison
pros.example: excluding MMLU test n-grams from pretraining reduces contamination-inflated scores by 3-8%

cons.claim: Over-aggressive decontamination may remove legitimately relevant training signal
cons.example: removing all n-gram matches can eliminate valuable domain knowledge text

failure_modes: decontaminating validation split but not test split
not reporting clean vs contaminated score pair
dynamic eval set not validated for difficulty parity
acceptance_tests: clean/contaminated score pair reported for all benchmarks
decontamination pipeline removes test n-grams from training before model training
held-out variant difficulty verified against original benchmark
revisit_triggers: new benchmark variant becomes community standard

nodes.definition: Select appropriate pass@k, accuracy@k, or coverage@k metric for the task; choose k based on inference budget and deployment context; apply unbiased estimators and specify confidence intervals for reported metrics.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: deployment k constraint changes or new unbiased estimator published

pros.claim: Unbiased pass@k estimator from Chen 2021 enables low-variance estimates with modest sample count
pros.example: pass@1 estimated from 200 samples is more reliable than greedy pass@1 from 50 samples

cons.claim: High k requires many inference samples, multiplying compute cost
cons.example: pass@100 on HumanEval requires 100x inference vs pass@1

failure_modes: using biased pass@k estimator (max over k)
not reporting k alongside metric
inappropriate k for deployment context (k=1 model tested at k=100)
acceptance_tests: pass@k uses unbiased estimator
k value documented alongside metric
95% confidence intervals reported for all pass@k metrics
revisit_triggers: new task type added requiring different metric

nodes.definition: Measure model calibration: expected calibration error (ECE), reliability diagrams, temperature scaling effect; evaluate whether model confidence scores align with empirical accuracy; report calibration alongside accuracy.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new calibration metric becomes standard or deployment risk tolerance changes

pros.claim: ECE reveals overconfident models that appear accurate but are unsafe in high-stakes decisions
pros.example: model with 75% accuracy and ECE=0.15 is less trustworthy than 73% accuracy and ECE=0.02

cons.claim: ECE is sensitive to bin count and calibration set distribution; requires large held-out set
cons.example: ECE with 10 bins vs 15 bins can differ significantly on small evaluation sets

failure_modes: reporting accuracy without calibration for safety-critical deployment
computing ECE on training distribution vs shifted deployment distribution
acceptance_tests: ECE computed with at least 1000 samples
reliability diagram visualized with documented bin count
calibration set distinct from accuracy evaluation set

nodes.definition: Critically interpret leaderboard rankings: detect Goodhart's law (metric becomes target), assess aggregate vs task-specific performance, account for evaluation setup differences, identify cherry-picking, and contextualize rankings within deployment requirements.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: leaderboard manipulation detected or evaluation community norms change

pros.claim: Task-specific re-ranking prevents deploying models optimized for benchmark overfitting
pros.example: MMLU rank 1 model may rank 5th on deployment-relevant clinical QA task

cons.claim: Leaderboard re-interpretation requires deep methodology knowledge; errors mislead decisions
cons.example: incorrect protocol comparison leads to wrong model selection for production

failure_modes: treating aggregate leaderboard rank as deployment rank
ignoring evaluation setup differences between leaderboard entries
not checking for cherry-picked benchmark subsets
acceptance_tests: deployment-relevant task identified and mapped to benchmark subsets
evaluation setup differences documented for compared models
Goodhart flags documented for top-ranked models
revisit_triggers: new benchmark optimization paper targeting current top benchmark

nodes.definition: Design and maintain held-out test sets: strict train/dev/test splits, access control, version-locked evaluation, canary test injection, split size adequacy for statistical power, and protocol for releasing evaluation only after model is frozen.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: test set access policy change or canary detection triggers

pros.claim: Locked test sets prevent adaptive overfitting and maintain evaluation integrity over model iterations
pros.example: private test set used only at final model freeze prevents 50+ rounds of adaptive tuning

cons.claim: Overly small test sets lack statistical power to distinguish close model performances
cons.example: 200-example test set has +/-3.5% accuracy confidence interval, masking real improvements

failure_modes: sharing test set with training pipeline developers
insufficient test set size for statistical significance
not locking test set version before evaluation campaign
acceptance_tests: test set inaccessible to model training team until evaluation complete
statistical power analysis confirms 80% power to detect 2% accuracy difference
canary examples injected and detected in any evaluation run that has access violation
revisit_triggers: canary example detected in model output
test set size insufficient for new task granularity

nodes.definition: Apply statistical significance testing to benchmark comparisons: bootstrap confidence intervals, McNemar's test, paired t-tests, effect size reporting (Cohen's d); account for multiple comparisons correction (Bonferroni, BH); assess practical vs statistical significance.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: statistical methodology norms change in NLP community

pros.claim: Statistical significance testing prevents spurious conclusions from small eval set differences
pros.example: McNemar test on HumanEval shows 1.5% pass@1 difference not significant at n=164 problems

cons.claim: Multiple comparison correction reduces power when comparing many benchmarks simultaneously
cons.example: Bonferroni correction on 50 benchmarks makes 3% improvement non-significant

failure_modes: reporting point estimates without confidence intervals
p-hacking by selecting favorable subsets post-hoc
ignoring practical significance even when statistical significance achieved
acceptance_tests: all comparisons report 95% confidence intervals
multiple comparison correction applied when testing >5 hypotheses
effect sizes reported alongside p-values

nodes.definition: Assess and mitigate prompt sensitivity in benchmark evaluation: measure score variance across prompt template variations, example ordering, and instruction phrasing; report robustness as metric alongside accuracy; standardize prompt templates.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new evidence of high prompt sensitivity for key benchmark published

pros.claim: Prompt sensitivity analysis reveals brittle models that appear strong only on carefully chosen prompts
pros.example: GSM8K score variance of +/-8% across 5 templates reveals fragile reasoning vs robust model

cons.claim: Full sensitivity analysis multiplies inference cost by number of template variants
cons.example: testing 10 template variants increases inference budget 10x

failure_modes: cherry-picking best-performing prompt template for reported score
not reporting variance metrics alongside accuracy
missing sensitivity analysis for instruction-tuned models
acceptance_tests: minimum 5 prompt template variants tested per benchmark
variance metric reported alongside mean score
standard template specified for cross-model comparison
revisit_triggers: community identifies new prompt sensitivity issue for key benchmark
model architecture change alters prompt sensitivity profile

nodes.definition: Design task-specific held-out evaluation benchmarks when existing public benchmarks are misaligned to deployment: annotation guidelines, inter-annotator agreement, difficulty stratification, domain representativeness, and update cadence.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: deployment task scope changes or domain distribution shifts

pros.claim: Custom benchmarks measure exactly the deployment-relevant capability with no proxy gap
pros.example: clinical note summarization benchmark directly measures patient safety-relevant accuracy

cons.claim: Custom benchmark creation is expensive and risks labeler-model agreement bias
cons.example: 1000-example medical QA benchmark costs 20K in expert annotation

failure_modes: benchmark too easy due to inadequate difficulty stratification
low IAA (<0.7 Cohen kappa) invalidates labels
benchmark scope creep misaligning to deployment task
acceptance_tests: inter-annotator agreement kappa>0.7 for all label types
difficulty strata documented with target distribution
domain coverage verified against deployment traffic sample
revisit_triggers: IAA drops below threshold on new annotation batch

nodes.definition: Evaluate model robustness: out-of-distribution (OOD) performance, adversarial perturbation tolerance, distribution shift evaluation (WILDS, PromptBench), checklist-style behavioral testing; measure performance degradation under realistic distribution shifts.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new distribution shift benchmark released or deployment OOD issue observed

pros.claim: OOD evaluation predicts real-world performance degradation under natural distribution shifts
pros.example: WILDS benchmark predicts production accuracy drop from lab to clinical domain

cons.claim: Adversarial robustness metrics may not correlate with natural robustness under benign distribution shifts
cons.example: adversarial perturbation tolerance and OOD accuracy are often uncorrelated

failure_modes: conflating adversarial robustness with natural robustness
not measuring performance on target deployment domain as OOD test
acceptance_tests: OOD evaluation includes deployment-relevant domain shift
behavioral test suite covers known failure modes
robustness score reported as accuracy gap (in-dist minus OOD)
revisit_triggers: new distribution shift detected in production
deployment domain expands to new distribution

nodes.definition: Apply LLM-as-judge evaluation for open-ended tasks (MT-Bench, AlpacaEval, Arena): judge model selection, position bias mitigation, self-evaluation bias, agreement with human raters, consistency checks; interpret win rates and ELO scores.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: judge model capability changes or new bias discovered in judge evaluation

pros.claim: LLM judge enables scalable open-ended evaluation at fraction of human annotation cost
pros.example: GPT-4 judge agreement with human on MT-Bench is 80%+, enabling cheap instruction-following eval

cons.claim: LLM judge exhibits position bias, length bias, and self-enhancement bias distorting win rates
cons.example: GPT-4 judges prefer longer responses even when shorter is correct; biases model development toward verbosity

failure_modes: using judge that was fine-tuned on same RLHF data as evaluated model (self-enhancement)
not measuring position bias (response A vs B order)
reporting win rates without human correlation validation
acceptance_tests: judge model distinct from evaluated model and its variants
position bias measured and swapped-order evaluation conducted
judge-human agreement measured on 200+ sample with Cohen kappa reported

nodes.definition: Manage evaluation compute budget: benchmark prioritization by signal-to-cost ratio, adaptive evaluation (early stopping), cached inference, efficient batch sizes, estimating score from subset via stratified sampling; balance eval breadth vs cost.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: compute budget changes or new efficient evaluation method published

pros.claim: Stratified subset sampling with 20% of examples provides 95% correlation with full evaluation
pros.example: 1000-example MMLU subset correlates r=0.98 with full 14K-example evaluation

cons.claim: Subset evaluation may miss tail distribution failures not captured in stratified sample
cons.example: 5% of benchmark examples contain adversarial difficulty; subset may under-sample

failure_modes: non-stratified random subset losing rare difficulty distribution
caching inference from different checkpoint versions
skipping important benchmarks to save compute
acceptance_tests: subset evaluation correlation validated on held-out model pair
cached inferences verified to match checkpoint version
cost-benefit reported for each benchmark in suite

nodes.definition: Ensure evaluation reproducibility: version-pin model, harness, dataset, and random seeds; artifact storage; evaluation logging; re-run validation; document hardware environment; enable public result reproduction via eval card.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new eval framework version released or reproducibility failure discovered

pros.claim: Version-pinned evaluation enables exact reproduction months later for comparison baselines
pros.example: pinning lm-eval v0.4.2 + model SHA ensures identical scores across labs reproducing results

cons.claim: Strict versioning creates maintenance burden when harness or model APIs change
cons.example: pinned harness version incompatible with new model API requires fork maintenance

failure_modes: floating harness version in requirements.txt
not logging random seeds
omitting hardware spec from eval card
acceptance_tests: eval card contains model SHA, harness version, dataset version, seeds, hardware spec
re-run of evaluation produces identical results
all eval artifacts stored in version-controlled artifact store

nodes.definition: Design aggregate scoring across diverse benchmark tasks: macro vs micro averaging, task-weighting strategies, normalization to chance baseline, aggregate score interpretability, and risk of aggregate hiding per-task regressions.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: task weighting policy changes or new task added to aggregate

pros.claim: Chance-normalized aggregate scores enable meaningful comparison across tasks with different random baselines
pros.example: normalizing MMLU (25% chance) and GSM8K (0% chance) to same scale before aggregating

cons.claim: Aggregate score can mask per-task regressions where improvement on one task hides degradation on another
cons.example: model improves MMLU 2% but regresses GSM8K 5%; aggregate shows +0.5% masking regression

failure_modes: not normalizing to chance baseline before averaging
aggregate hides safety-critical per-task regression
task weighting not documented or arbitrary
acceptance_tests: all tasks normalized to chance baseline before aggregation
per-task breakdown always reported alongside aggregate
regression alert fires when any task drops >2% from previous version

nodes.definition: Integrate evaluation into CI/CD: automated eval triggers on model checkpoint commits, regression gates blocking release on performance drop, eval dashboards, alert thresholds, and scheduled full-suite evaluation cadence.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: CI system changed or evaluation threshold policy updated

pros.claim: Automated regression gates prevent releasing model checkpoints with performance degradation
pros.example: CI eval gate catches 3% GSM8K regression before model promotion to staging

cons.claim: Automated eval in CI increases wall-clock time per commit cycle; fast subset eval may miss regression
cons.example: 5-minute subset eval missing 1% regression that full eval would catch

failure_modes: regression gate threshold set too loose (>5% drop allowed)
eval CI not triggered on every checkpoint
eval pipeline failure treated as passing gate
acceptance_tests: CI triggers evaluation on every model checkpoint commit
regression gate blocks release if any tracked metric drops >2%
eval pipeline failure alerts on-call engineer and blocks release

edges.resolution_rule: Treat leaderboard scores as hypothesis not ground truth; re-run on held-out task-specific benchmark before accepting rank
Contaminated benchmark excluded from primary evaluation or replaced with dynamic variant; contamination fraction documented
High sensitivity triggers mandatory multi-template evaluation; single-template score flagged as fragile
LLM judge win rates complement not replace functional pass@k; both reported for tasks where both apply
Compute constraint drives benchmark prioritization; document which benchmarks skipped and estimated coverage loss

conflict_axes.name: benchmark_coverage_vs_compute_cost
conflict_axes.description: Broader benchmark coverage improves evaluation validity but multiplies compute and latency cost
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: prioritize benchmarks by signal-to-cost ratio; use stratified subset for development and full suite for final evaluation

conflict_axes.name: few_shot_vs_zero_shot_fairness
conflict_axes.description: Few-shot prompting inflates scores for base models vs instruction-tuned models on same benchmark; protocol choice affects cross-model comparison validity
conflict_axes.pole_b: per-model optimal protocol for maximum performance
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: document protocol per model type; never mix protocols in cross-model comparison; report both when comparing base vs instruction-tuned

conflict_axes.name: public_benchmark_availability_vs_contamination_risk
conflict_axes.description: Public benchmarks enable community comparison but create contamination risk when test sets appear in training corpora
conflict_axes.pole_a: public standard benchmarks for community comparability
conflict_axes.pole_b: private held-out sets immune to contamination
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: use public benchmarks with contamination check + private held-out task-specific set for final deployment evaluation

conflict_axes.name: aggregate_score_vs_per_task_regression_visibility
conflict_axes.description: Aggregate leaderboard scores hide per-task regressions; fine-grained breakdowns obscure overall trends
conflict_axes.pole_a: single aggregate score for leaderboard simplicity
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: always report per-task breakdown alongside aggregate; regression gates monitor both aggregate and per-task thresholds

conflict_axes.name: goodhart_law_benchmark_optimization
conflict_axes.description: Optimizing models directly toward benchmark scores causes Goodhart's law; benchmarks cease to measure intended capability
conflict_axes.pole_a: optimize model on benchmark signals for best leaderboard rank
conflict_axes.pole_b: treat benchmark as held-out unseen evaluation only
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: separate benchmark evaluation from training signal; rotate benchmarks periodically; use dynamic evaluation for safety-critical capability

conflict_axes.name: llm_judge_scalability_vs_bias
conflict_axes.description: LLM-as-judge enables scalable evaluation of open-ended outputs but introduces position, length, and self-enhancement biases
conflict_axes.pole_a: scalable LLM judge for all open-ended evaluation
conflict_axes.pole_b: human evaluation only for unbiased but costly assessment
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: use LLM judge for relative ranking with bias mitigations; validate against human labels on 10% sample; report human-judge agreement

conflict_axes.name: statistical_vs_practical_significance
conflict_axes.description: Statistical significance with large evaluation sets can flag trivially small differences as significant; practical significance requires effect size judgment
conflict_axes.pole_a: report all statistically significant results as meaningful
conflict_axes.pole_b: require practical significance threshold for deployment decisions
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: require both statistical significance (p<0.05) and practical significance (effect size > deployment threshold) for model promotion

conflict_axes.name: evaluation_reproducibility_vs_rapid_iteration
conflict_axes.description: Strict versioning and reproducibility requirements slow iteration speed; rapid development benefits from flexible evaluation but risks irreproducible results
conflict_axes.pole_a: strict reproducibility with pinned versions and full documentation
conflict_axes.pole_b: fast iteration with approximate evaluation and loose versioning
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: lightweight subset eval for rapid iteration; full reproducible eval gated on checkpoint promotion; never report results without versioned artifact

conflict_axes.name: task_specific_benchmark_vs_public_comparability
conflict_axes.description: Custom task-specific benchmarks maximize deployment relevance but prevent direct comparison to published results
conflict_axes.pole_a: fully custom benchmarks for maximum deployment relevance
conflict_axes.pole_b: public standard benchmarks for external comparability
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: run both public and custom benchmarks; use public for external positioning; use custom for internal deployment decision-making

conflict_axes.name: prompt_sensitivity_budget_vs_robustness_measurement
conflict_axes.description: Measuring prompt sensitivity requires running multiple template variants, multiplying inference cost; single-template eval is cheap but hides robustness gaps
conflict_axes.pole_a: full prompt sensitivity analysis (10+ templates per benchmark)
conflict_axes.pole_b: single canonical template for cost efficiency
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: run sensitivity analysis during benchmark selection phase; for stable benchmarks use canonical template; re-run sensitivity when model architecture changes

edge_cases.description: Model scores at ceiling (>90%) on benchmark
edge_cases.resolution: retire benchmark or add harder variant; document saturation; switch to harder benchmark (MATH, ARC-Challenge)

edge_cases.description: Contamination fraction exceeds 20% of test set
edge_cases.trigger: n-gram overlap check reveals >20% test set in training data
edge_cases.resolution: exclude benchmark from primary evaluation; use clean subset only; document publicly; add held-out replacement

edge_cases.trigger: evaluated model wins vs judge model variant at rate >80% on equal outputs
edge_cases.resolution: replace judge with model from different family; conduct swap-order experiment; weight human labels higher

edge_cases.description: Prompt template change causes >5% score shift on same model
edge_cases.trigger: template A vs template B difference exceeds 5 percentage points on same model same benchmark
edge_cases.resolution: flag benchmark as high prompt-sensitivity; report with template variance; use median across template variants

edge_cases.description: Evaluation harness version update shifts baseline scores
edge_cases.trigger: lm-eval-harness minor version update causes >1% change on pinned reference model
edge_cases.resolution: pin harness version for all runs in comparison; document version delta; re-evaluate baselines with new version before promotion

edge_cases.description: Inter-annotator agreement below 0.7 kappa on custom benchmark
edge_cases.trigger: IAA kappa drops below 0.7 in custom benchmark annotation batch
edge_cases.resolution: halt annotation; revise guidelines; retrain annotators; discard low-agreement batch; increase example clarity

edge_cases.description: Aggregate score improves while safety-critical task regresses
edge_cases.trigger: aggregate score increases but toxicity or fairness metric worsens
edge_cases.resolution: block model promotion; require all safety-critical tasks to be non-regressive before aggregate score considered

edge_cases.description: Statistical power insufficient to distinguish models at target delta
edge_cases.trigger: confidence interval width exceeds practical significance threshold on evaluation set
edge_cases.resolution: increase evaluation set size; use more powerful test (McNemar on paired items); document uncertainty explicitly

edge_cases.description: Sandbox escape in HumanEval code execution
edge_cases.trigger: model generates code that escapes sandboxed execution environment
edge_cases.resolution: enforce strict sandbox (gVisor, Docker with seccomp); block network access; rate-limit file system; log all executions

edge_cases.description: Goodhart gaming: model scores plateau on training benchmarks while deployment performance drops
edge_cases.trigger: benchmark score trend diverges from downstream deployment quality metrics by >10%
edge_cases.resolution: rotate held-out benchmarks; add dynamic evaluation; measure deployment proxy metric directly; reduce training signal from benchmark

edge_cases.description: OOD distribution shift causes >15% accuracy drop in production
edge_cases.trigger: production accuracy metric drops >15% vs in-distribution eval
edge_cases.resolution: trigger OOD evaluation suite; add shifted-domain examples to evaluation; update held-out benchmark to cover new distribution

edge_cases.description: Evaluation CI pipeline failure silently blocks all model releases
edge_cases.trigger: eval infrastructure failure causes CI to report false pass or block all releases
edge_cases.resolution: implement fallback to last known good eval; page on-call; never treat pipeline failure as passing gate

workflow.description: Map deployment capability axes to benchmark suite; cover reasoning, knowledge, code, and safety dimensions
Run 8-gram overlap check of training corpus against all benchmark test splits before any evaluation
Exclude contaminated benchmarks or restrict to clean subsets; flag for public reporting
Fix shot count, template, and example selection strategy; document per benchmark and model type
Pin lm-eval-harness version; configure model integration; set batch size and generation params
Execute MMLU, GSM8K, BBH, HumanEval with standardized protocol; record per-task scores
Run 5+ template variants on subset; compute variance; flag high-sensitivity benchmarks
Normalize to chance baseline; compute macro-average aggregate; check per-task regression against previous checkpoint
Apply McNemar or bootstrap CI for model comparisons; apply multiple comparison correction; report effect sizes
Run HELM suite for calibration, fairness, robustness, and toxicity metrics alongside accuracy
Map leaderboard scores to deployment-relevant task ranking; document Goodhart risks; check methodology consistency
Commit eval card with model SHA, harness version, dataset version, seeds, hardware; store versioned artifacts

dominance_rules.rule: Contamination check before any evaluation report
dominance_rules.condition: any benchmark result to be published or used in model selection
dominance_rules.action: CONTAMINATION_DETECTION must complete and contaminated benchmarks excluded before BENCH_SELECTION is finalized
dominance_rules.rationale: Contaminated benchmark results are invalid and cannot be corrected post-publication

dominance_rules.rule: Human review required for high-risk evaluation decisions
dominance_rules.rationale: High-risk evaluation nodes gate model deployment; automated checks insufficient

dominance_rules.rule: Version pinning mandatory before result reporting
dominance_rules.condition: evaluation results to be stored or shared
dominance_rules.action: EVAL_REPRODUCIBILITY must be satisfied; harness, model, dataset versions logged
dominance_rules.rationale: Non-reproducible results cannot be compared or audited

dominance_rules.rule: Regression gate blocks release on any tracked metric drop
dominance_rules.action: EVAL_PIPELINE_CI regression gate must pass; no metric may drop >2% from previous approved checkpoint
dominance_rules.rationale: Aggregate score improvement never justifies per-task safety regression

dominance_rules.rule: Protocol consistency mandatory for cross-model comparison
dominance_rules.condition: comparison involves models from different families or training regimes
dominance_rules.action: FEWSHOT_ZEROSHOT protocol must be identical for all compared models; mixing protocols invalidates comparison
dominance_rules.rationale: Protocol difference is confounded with model capability difference

dominance_rules.rule: Safety-critical tasks block aggregate score from hiding regression
dominance_rules.action: model promotion blocked regardless of aggregate score improvement
dominance_rules.rationale: Safety regressions are categorically non-negotiable regardless of accuracy gains

dominance_rules.rule: Statistical significance required for model promotion decisions
dominance_rules.condition: comparing two model checkpoints for promotion
dominance_rules.action: STATISTICAL_SIGNIFICANCE must show p<0.05 and practical significance for all promotion-driving metrics
dominance_rules.rationale: Point estimates without significance testing lead to spurious promotions from noise

dominance_rules.rule: Custom benchmark IAA must be validated before use in model selection
dominance_rules.condition: HELDOUT_BENCHMARK_DESIGN output used for model selection
dominance_rules.action: IAA kappa must exceed 0.7; low-agreement batches excluded
dominance_rules.rationale: Low-IAA labels introduce noise that makes model comparisons unreliable

dominance_rules.rule: Goodhart detection supersedes leaderboard rank for deployment decisions
dominance_rules.action: require deployment-specific task evaluation; leaderboard rank treated as prior not evidence
dominance_rules.rationale: Goodhart-gamed benchmarks measure optimization pressure not capability

dominance_rules.condition: HumanEval or any code execution benchmark run
dominance_rules.action: sandboxed execution environment verified before any model code runs
dominance_rules.rationale: Unsandboxed code execution from model outputs creates security vulnerability

anti_rework_rules.rule: Lock benchmark suite before contamination check
anti_rework_rules.rationale: Running contamination check after benchmark swap wastes the check; suite must be fixed first

anti_rework_rules.rule: Pin eval harness version before any cross-model comparison
anti_rework_rules.rationale: Harness version change after comparison started requires re-running all baselines

anti_rework_rules.rule: Fix shot count before running sensitivity analysis
anti_rework_rules.rationale: Changing shot count after sensitivity analysis invalidates variance estimates
Security incident during eval requires full restart and security audit

anti_rework_rules.rule: Conduct statistical power analysis before collecting evaluation set
anti_rework_rules.rationale: Undersized test set discovered post-collection requires expensive re-annotation
Scaling annotation with low IAA wastes budget; guideline revision requires re-annotation

anti_rework_rules.rule: Agree on aggregation strategy before benchmark execution
anti_rework_rules.rationale: Changing macro vs micro averaging after scores collected requires justification audit

anti_rework_rules.rule: Configure regression gate thresholds before first CI eval run
anti_rework_rules.rationale: Changing thresholds retroactively creates cherry-picking risk

anti_rework_rules.rule: Validate judge-human agreement before LLM-judge campaign
anti_rework_rules.rationale: Discovering low agreement post-campaign requires expensive human re-annotation

anti_rework_rules.rule: Document protocol differences before cross-leaderboard comparison
anti_rework_rules.rationale: Retroactive protocol documentation cannot fix invalid comparisons already published

iteration_protocol.trigger: benchmark score plateau or ceiling effect
iteration_protocol.action: replace with harder benchmark variant; document saturation; update BENCH_SELECTION

iteration_protocol.trigger: contamination fraction increases in new training data
iteration_protocol.action: re-run CONTAMINATION_DETECTION on new corpus; update CONTAMINATION_MITIGATION; refresh clean benchmark list

iteration_protocol.trigger: prompt sensitivity variance exceeds 5% on core benchmark
iteration_protocol.action: run full template sensitivity analysis; standardize canonical template; update FEWSHOT_ZEROSHOT spec
iteration_protocol.frequency: on architecture or training regime change

iteration_protocol.action: evaluate version delta on reference model; update pinned version; re-run baselines with new version

iteration_protocol.trigger: regression alert fires in CI evaluation
iteration_protocol.action: root-cause per-task regression; determine if algorithmic or data regression; block promotion until resolved
investigate judge bias; update judge model or bias mitigation; re-evaluate last 4 weeks of LLM-judge results

iteration_protocol.trigger: deployment distribution shift detected in production
iteration_protocol.action: add OOD benchmark covering new distribution; update ROBUSTNESS_EVAL suite; re-evaluate model

iteration_protocol.trigger: new community benchmark standardized by field consensus
iteration_protocol.action: evaluate adoption cost vs coverage benefit; add to suite or replace outdated benchmark
retire targeted benchmark; add dynamic evaluation variant; increase held-out test set diversity

priority_rationale.BENCH_SELECTION: All evaluation depends on benchmark selection; must be decided first
priority_rationale.CONTAMINATION_DETECTION: Contamination invalidates all results; must run before any eval report
priority_rationale.HELD_OUT_TESTSET: Test set integrity is prerequisite for valid model comparison
priority_rationale.FEWSHOT_ZEROSHOT: Protocol standardization gates all cross-model comparisons
priority_rationale.CONTAMINATION_MITIGATION: Must follow detection; gates final benchmark list
priority_rationale.HUMANEVAL_PROTOCOL: High-value code eval with security requirements
priority_rationale.MMLU_PROTOCOL: Primary knowledge benchmark; gates aggregate score
priority_rationale.METRIC_AT_K: Metric definition gates all quantitative comparisons
priority_rationale.HELM_FRAMEWORK: Holistic eval for safety and fairness dimensions
priority_rationale.JUDGE_MODEL_EVAL: Scalable open-ended eval; high bias risk
priority_rationale.LEADERBOARD_INTERPRETATION: Contextualizes all results for deployment decisions
priority_rationale.EVAL_COST_COMPUTE: Resource optimization; downstream of core methodology

change_control.review_cadence: quarterly or on material model architecture change
